text:
harper_sec: opening thread - we had a weird suppression today where the DAST auto-suppression accepted a finding because CI reported a decrypt, but audit logs show no KMS Decrypt for the key version that actually performed the decrypt. sounds like key rotation happened mid-run. thoughts? :eyes:
diego_dev: yep saw it. our keystore rotates key versions every 24h and there was a rotation 2s before the decrypt. CI used the new key version locally but central logs only retained entries under the old key name for a short TTL.
paul_sre: that explains mismatch. audit rows reference full resource name including keyVersion, so if the rotation happened and the sink filters by key resource with previous name we might miss it. also some sinks were configured to filter by keyRing only.
nina_cloud: two immediate asks: (1) make premerge gating tolerant of key-version churn (don't require exact key version match; allow keyRing-level Decrypt rows within window), (2) consider adding a non-repudiable attestation artifact from CI that references the exact key version used so security can verify even if logs are delayed.
harper_sec: +1. proposal: update the GH Action gate to query for Decrypt events on either the specific keyVersion OR the parent keyRing for a +/-60s window. fallback to evidence attestation if none found.
diego_dev: on attestation: we can add a tiny SLSA-style statement after decrypt that contains: repo, commit, run-id, keyResource, keyVersion, and a signature created by an ephemeral signing key that is itself attested by the keystore service. we already rotate the keystore ephemeral signing key per day.
paul_sre: curious: who verifies the signature? security wants to avoid granting KMS decrypt/list perms to sec-team. they prefer verifying signed metadata and reading logs only. if the keystore can publish a short-lived certificate chain (or Rekor entry) proving the signing key was issued by keystore-service, sec can validate without extra kms perms.
ina_cloud: exactly. suggest using an internal rekor-like transparency log (we already have an internal ledger service) where the keystore posts a hash of the attestation. GH Action would upload the attestation blob and ledger entry ID to the evidence-bundle. security then verifies blob signature and ledger ID matches. no additional cloudkms roles needed for sec.
harper_sec: nice. operationally we need: (A) premerge gate: check BQ log for Decrypt on keyRing OR check evidence-bundle attest signature+ledger entry, (B) RBAC: grant sec-team BigQuery DataViewer on the audit dataset but not cloudkms roles, (C) infra: ensure logging sinks include DATA_ACCESS for KMS key projects and don't filter out keyVersion.
diego_dev: implementation sketch for attestation JSON: `{"run_id":"$RUN_ID","commit":"$SHA","key":"projects/p/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/deploy-key","key_version":"1","timestamp":"..."}` then keystore-service signs it and returns `attestation.sig` and `ledger_id`. GH Action uploads both to gs://sdlc-evidence/$REPO/$RUN_ID/ and the premerge check picks them up.
paul_sre: small caveat: attackers who control CI runner could fake attestations unless the keystore only signs after performing an authenticated decrypt. keystore should only sign if the decrypt succeeded and the caller authenticated via Workload Identity; attestation must include KMS operation nonce or audit digest.
nina_cloud: agree — design rule: keystore signs attestation only server-side after performing decrypt; signing key is never exposed to runners. attestation should include a monotonic operation id that appears in KMS audit row when available. that links artifact -> audit row.
harper_sec: infra tasks: (1) update sink filters to not drop keyVersion-level rows, (2) create BigQuery dataset `sdlc.decrypts` with 90d partition retention and grant sec-team DataViewer, (3) implement attestation endpoint in keystore-service and ledger posting. I'll file SEC-1345.
slsa-bot: [auto] created ticket SEC-1345: "sdlc: attestation + key-rotation tolerant decrypt evidence and RBAC plan" assigned to @harper_sec. link: https://github.internal/redwood/security/SEC-1345
diego_dev: UX for premerge: GH Action should wait 45s after job end, query BigQuery for `protoPayload.methodName="google.crypto.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND (resource.labels.keyVersionId="$KEYVER" OR resource.labels.keyRingId="$KEYRING")`, if empty fetch evidence-bundle and validate signature+ledger_id. set GitHub check `sdlc/kms-audit` to pending->success/failure and attach artifacts.
paul_sre: monitoring: emit metric `sdlc.missing_decrypt_evidence_total` when both BQ and attestation checks fail. if it spikes after rollout, we should revisit grant TTL and sink replication tuning.
harper_sec: RBAC note: for minimal blast radius, sec-team gets only BigQuery read on `sdlc.decrypts` dataset and access to the evidence-bucket `gs://sdlc-evidence` with objectViewer. no cloudkms roles. operational security happy?
nina_cloud: yes, that keeps separation. last item: add runbook steps: if evidence missing, sec oncall should (1) query BigQuery manually, (2) request keystore-service to reissue attestation for run-id (if allowed), (3) if still missing escalate to infra and dev owners for timeline reconstruction. I'll add to the runbook in SEC-1345.
harper_sec: great. i'll own SEC-1345 and the GH Action PR to implement the dual-check behavior. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
